plan: This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - I don't need to worry about winning too much because I only pay what the second-highest bidder bid, not my own bid. If I win, my profit is my value minus the second-highest bid, which is maximized by bidding truthfully. My value is $4, so I'll bid exactly $4.

This is a second-price auction format where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. If I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $23.

This is a second-price auction format where I pay the second-highest bid if I win. The dominant strategy in this type of auction is to bid my true value, as this ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids (profitable) and lose when it doesn't (avoiding losses). Bidding above my value risks negative profit if I win at a price above my value. Bidding below risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history, I'll bid my true value of $32.
